summary.headline: MAS Financial Q2 FY27 consolidated AUM rose 23.3% to INR 17,042 crores; PAT grew about 26% to INR 115 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated AUM crossed INR 17,000 crores, up 23.3% YoY, and consolidated quarterly PAT was INR 115 crores, up about 26%. Standalone PAT was INR 110.05 crores (+22.7%) and standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, unchanged QoQ, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.63% from 2.58%. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth and a 2.75-3% ROA band, flagged an expected 20-25 bps rise in cost of borrowing as RBI hiked repo, and kept credit-cost buffers elevated. Analysts pressed on rising GNPA, wheels weakness, SME stress and yield compression; management attributed most of this to seasoning and product mix.

segments.name: MFSL standalone
segments.commentary: Gross Stage 3 2.63% (Q1: 2.58%), net Stage 3 1.70% (unchanged); management overlay of INR 17 crores not netted off. Standalone PBT INR 147.38 crores (+22.58%).

segments.name: MAS Rural Housing (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM crossed INR 1,000 crores at INR 1,031.47 crores; Q2 PAT INR 4.62 crores (+54.71%). Gross Stage 3 0.99% (Q1: 0.98%), net Stage 3 0.70% (Q1: 0.68%); overlay INR 3.69 crores.

segments.name: MSME (MEL and SME)
segments.commentary: Flagship segment. Management said SME GNPA rose over the last three to four quarters due to book maturity; SME ticket size fell from about INR 35 lakh back to about INR 29 lakh, with a 6-12 quarter target of INR 35-45 lakh.

segments.name: Wheels (two-wheeler and commercial vehicle)
segments.commentary: Growth flattish; two-wheeler grew decently while CV growth is deliberately cautious. Wheels drove the uptick in 61-90 DPD and 91-120 DPD buckets. Wheels currently about 8-9% of AUM, targeted at 15-20% in 3-5 years.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Capped at 10% of total AUM; management said current share is about 9%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% YoY; management said H1 momentum should continue into H2 but growth could slow if opportunities are lacking.
ROA target maintained at 2.75-3%, despite margin pressure from rate hikes.
Cost of borrowing expected to rise 20-25 bps after repo hikes (25 bps done, another 25 bps expected in the year); analyst reconciled this to about 9.4-9.5%.
90+ DPD guided at 2.5-2.75% and net NPA below 2%.
Long-term aim of INR 1 lakh crore AUM by 2036; INR 20,000 crores AUM expected by year-end; medium-term INR 30,000-35,000 crores cited.
Branch count guided to rise from about 210 to around 300 over roughly two years; centres up about 1,000 in the last four to five quarters.
Off-book (direct assignment) share to be held at 20-25%, versus 17% currently; assignment range 20-22% indicated.
capex_capacity: Average on-balance-sheet liquidity about INR 1,000 crores; cash credit lines about INR 1,500 crores across 12 banks, utilised 80-85%.
Sanctions in hand exceed INR 2,500 crores; company said it is tied up for the full year.
Q2 long-term borrowing about INR 1,195 crores (term loans, NCDs INR 575 crores, ECB USD 25 million); sanctioned long-term lines about INR 1,500 crores.
Direct assignments of about INR 850 crores in Q2; a further INR 850 crores sanctioned for execution in Q3.
Lateral hubs opened in Mumbai and Delhi for senior hires in sales, underwriting, operations and technology.
demand_pricing: Management said credit demand remains strong; lower sanction rates are being offset by higher demand.
Analyst asked about drought in 5-6 states: about 10% of the portfolio sits in drought-declared states, but direct agri exposure is under 1%; management saw no SME stress yet.
Asset mix: about 65-70% fixed-rate, 30% floating; liabilities about 20% fixed, about 50% MCLR-linked (mostly 1-year), with the rest repo-linked and reset every 3 months.
Q2 yield on loans 16.08% vs 16.17% in Q1 (about 9 bps decline, attributed to product mix); analyst's 58 bps figure to be reconciled offline.
Distribution: direct about 68% of AUM, DSA/NBFC partners about 32%.

qa_highlights.question: Are drought-hit states causing SME cash-flow stress and what is the agri exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no SME stress as demand is continuous and financials are reviewed; direct agri is under 1% and about 10% of the portfolio is in drought-declared states.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fixed vs MCLR split of borrowings and how will margins hold up?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20% fixed (mainly capital market borrowings and some term loans), about 50% MCLR-linked mostly 1-year; margins to be protected by bargaining on spreads, repricing floating assets (about 30%) and short-tenure loans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA rising for 12 quarters and where will it stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasoning of the retail book (mix moved from 40/60 to 30/68), high-loss wheels and MSME stress over 1-1.5 years; 90+ DPD guided at 2.5-2.75%.

qa_highlights.question: Why does credit cost look high versus the asset-quality trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it deliberately built extra provisions in Stage 2 and Stage 3 this year as a buffer, which lifts credit cost without disturbing ROA; buffers may be released if NIM pressure is high and conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for wheels and CV growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Wheels growth flat; CV caution continues while distribution and manpower are rebuilt, with pickup expected in 2-3 quarters; the aim is to grow wheels to 15-20% of AUM in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why has SME ticket size declined and what are the restrictions?
qa_highlights.answer: Ticket size fell from about INR 35 lakh to INR 29 lakh; management is cautious on import-export, transport/logistics and some metal businesses, with changes described as incremental.

risks_watch: Rising GNPA and wheels asset quality; gross Stage 3 rose to 2.63% and 61-120 DPD buckets increased.
Cost of borrowing rising 20-25 bps against a 2.75-3% ROA target; yield pressure with about 9 bps decline in Q2.
SME book maturing with rising GNPA; ticket-size volatility.
El Nino and drought exposure, with about 10% of the portfolio in drought-declared states.
Management is not chasing growth; it is open to slowing if opportunities fall short.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, funding and capital (22.12% CRAR), but defensive on asset quality and margins, repeatedly reframing rising GNPA and provisions as seasoning and deliberate buffers. Several answers were deferred offline (58 bps yield reconciliation, write-off figures).
key_quotes: We have a capital adequacy of more than 22% giving us sufficient room to grow further.
we plan our activities in such a manner that we can maintain the ROAs between 2.75% to 3%.
2.58% to 2.62% should not be reckoned as a deterioration in the quality, nor 2.62% to 2.55% should be considered as an improvement in the quality.
our aim is to reach INR 1Lakh crore AUM by 2036.

adds.what: Branch network from about 210 to around 300 branches over roughly two years

growth.why: Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth (midpoint 22.5%) for FY27, backed by sanctions in hand above INR 2,500 crores, INR 850 crores of direct assignments sanctioned for Q3, and a branch expansion from about 210 to about 300 over roughly two years; the 20-25% range is guided but the branch timeline is long and the call flagged growth could slow without opportunities.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of borrowing guided up 20-25 bps after 25 bps repo hike (another 25 bps expected) and Q2 loan yield fell about 9 bps QoQ to 16.08%, so spreads face pressure despite the 2.75-3% ROA target being held.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches guided from about 210 to around 300 over roughly two years and about 1,000 centres added in the last four to five quarters, though no capex figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth guided at 20-25% YoY (midpoint 22.5%) with sanctions in hand above INR 2,500 crores and INR 850 crores of direct assignments sanctioned for Q3, but management said growth could slow without opportunities.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held (AUM 20-25%, ROA 2.75-3%) and cost of borrowing was raised, with no sign of a beat.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross Stage 3 rose to 2.63% from 2.58%, wheels and SME stress persist, 90+ DPD is guided at 2.5-2.75% and cost of borrowing is set to rise 20-25 bps against a held ROA target.

rows.label: Sanctions in hand above INR 2,500 crores for full year
rows.why: Sanctions above INR 2,500 crores are tied up for the full year, which supports the 20-25% AUM guide.

rows.label: Direct assignment and off-book share held at 20-25%
rows.why: Off-book share is 17% today with INR 850 crores of direct assignments sanctioned for Q3, and management committed to hold 20-25%.

rows.label: Spread defence and repricing of floating assets
rows.why: About 30% of assets are floating and management plans to protect margins by bargaining on spreads, but the 20-25 bps rise in borrowing cost is not yet offset.

tone.note: Management was confident on AUM growth, funding and 22.12% CRAR but defensive on rising GNPA, wheels and margins, attributing them to seasoning and deliberate buffers; analysts pressed on asset quality, SME stress and yield compression.
